cards.text: Israel is on the move again, traveling along the road to Atharim. Down in the Negev, a king hears they're coming. And friend, this king is NOT baking them a welcome batch.

cards.question: The king who hears that Israel is coming is the Canaanite king of ___.
When the king of Arad hears Israel is coming along the road to Atharim, he lets them pass by in peace.

cards.text: Nope. He attacks Israel. And when it's over, he doesn't go home empty-handed.

cards.question: What does the king of Arad take from Israel when he attacks?

cards.text: Some of Israel's own people? Captured. Taken. GONE. So Israel doesn't grab a plan first. They turn to the LORD.

cards.question: When Israel turns to the LORD after the attack from Arad, what do they do?
In Israel's vow, what do they ask the LORD to do?

answers.text: Deliver this people into their hands
Give them a safe road past Arad
Lead them far away from the Negev

cards.text: And if He does, here's Israel's side of the deal: "we will devote their cities to destruction." Friend, the biggest promise I make is "I'll stop eating the chocolate chips before they hit the dough." And I can't even keep THAT one.

cards.question: The LORD hears Israel's plea and delivers up the Canaanites.

cards.text: The LORD came through. Now the ball is in Israel's court.

cards.question: After the LORD delivers up the Canaanites, what does Israel do with the vow they made?

cards.text: Israel devotes the Canaanites and their cities to destruction, just like they said. Then they give the place a name.

cards.question: What does Israel name the place where the Canaanites of Arad were defeated?

findings.problem: The joke 'this king is NOT baking them a welcome batch' tells the baker the king is hostile. That gives away the answer to card 3, which asks whether he lets Israel pass in peace.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'So Israel doesn't grab a plan first. They turn to the LORD.' rules out the wrong answer 'They send out spies' on card 7, because sending spies is a plan.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card runs to six sentences or fragments ('Some of Israel's own people? Captured. Taken. GONE. So Israel doesn't grab a plan first. They turn to the LORD.') and carries two beats: the capture and the turn to the LORD.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'So Israel doesn't grab a plan first' adds something about Israel that the text doesn't say. Verse 2 only says Israel made a vow.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences: the vow quote, the chocolate chip promise, and 'And I can't even keep THAT one.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The chocolate chip joke comes right after Israel vows to devote cities to destruction. It doesn't target God or Scripture, but the light tone sits next to a grave vow.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin joke on the same card as a vow of destruction, or should humor stay away from devoting cities to destruction?
